draft.title: Nationalism and nation-states
card: Nationalism is the belief that people who share a language, history and culture should rule themselves as a nation. It gives people a sense of belonging to a larger group.
A nation-state is a country whose people share a national identity and rule themselves. In the 1800s nationalism helped to unite people who lived in many small states.
Italy and Germany each became a nation-state in the 1800s. Before this, each was a group of separate states.
Nationalism can also fuel rivalry between nations.
draft.remember: Nationalism ties people to their nation, and in the 1800s it helped to create nation-states such as Italy and Germany.

a.q: Which statement is the best example of nationalism?
opts: A people with one culture should rule themselves
A strong country should take over weaker lands
A people should be free to move wherever they like
A ruler should share power with an elected body
a.why: Nationalism is the belief that a people with a shared language, history and culture should rule themselves. The belief about taking over weaker lands is about ruling other peoples, not self-rule, so it is not nationalism.
a.clue: Look for the belief about a shared identity and self-rule.

b.q: Italy was once many small states. Which idea best explains why many people backed a single Italian nation-state?
opts: They saw themselves as one nation and wanted self-rule
They wanted their rulers to take over lands overseas
They hoped to keep their states separate from each other
They were made to move to Italy by other great powers
b.why: Many people shared a language, history and culture, so they saw themselves as one nation and wanted to rule themselves in one nation-state. Taking over lands overseas is about ruling other peoples, and keeping states separate is the opposite of unity.
b.clue: Think about what a shared language and history can lead people to want.

a.best: A people with one culture should rule themselves

b.best: They saw themselves as one nation and wanted self-rule
